groups.title: Section A · 第 1 篇 · 1–2 题
groups.material:
A JetBlue Airlines flight from West Palm Beach to New York City was forced to turn around and land Sunday morning after the plane struck a bird. The flight from Palm Beach International Airport to LaGuardia Airport turned around just minutes after takeoff following the strike.
No injuries were reported on the plane, and the flight took off once again 7.5 hours after the first attempt. "It was like a split second of panic…that resulted in this nervous reaction on the plane," said passenger Brian Healy. "There was total quiet, and then there was relief when the plane came to a stop." An email from JetBlue read, "Our team is working to accommodate customers on later flights."

groups.title: Section A · 第 2 篇 · 3–4 题
groups.material:
A deadly snake, which had finally been tracked down after escaping a zoo, has slipped away for the second time. The poisonous snake forced the closure of the attraction last week when staff noticed the disappearance.
After six days of desperate searching, he was eventually found and placed in a supposedly secure area. But it seems the animal is no fan of the zoo, because yet again he is out on the loose. The snake is a relative newcomer to the zoo but has already been frustrating its staff. The staff believe he squeezed himself out of a gap located around new energy-saving bulbs installed inside the snake house. He was only found the first time around because staff brought in a special machine to trace him inside a wall opening.
This kind of snake is one of the most deadly and poisonous in the wild, and they can range from 3 to 5 meters in length.

groups.title: Section A · 第 3 篇 · 5–7 题
groups.material:
Electric bikes have been the craze in downtown Jacksonville since they were first introduced earlier this month as a one-year pilot program. But they're leading to safety concerns, mainly at night when some riders don't follow the rules of the road.
As the night goes on, groups of riders are often seen traveling in just about every direction in the streets and on pedestrian paths. That is increasing the probability of dangerous accidents.
Electric bike riders have to follow all the same rules as you would if you were in an automobile. That means no running red lights or traveling in the opposite direction of traffic on one-way streets.
City Council Member Anna Cumber was instrumental in introducing the electric bikes to Jacksonville as a way to bring new life into downtown. And she's aware of the concerns. Cumber said, "People can have fun, but both drivers and riders are responsible for paying attention while on the road. And never assume the driver is going to stop or see you."

groups.title: Section B · 第 1 篇 · 8–11 题
groups.material:
M: What's the best way to teach children how to save and spend their money?
W: You should make money a regular topic of discussion. It's best to start young, so it's instinctive rather than a scary subject.
M: In our family, we talk openly about things like the budget for holidays, how taxes reduce your income, and how to shop around for the best deals.
W: Indeed. It's also essential to make money real for children through practical examples. Working out how much we save using discount pizza coupons, for example, is much more relevant than abstract sums.
M: We also give our kids pocket money, and the amount they get is linked to chores, such as putting the bins out and emptying the dishwasher.
W: We do that too, and it's paid according to their age. Two pounds for each year so they can see some progression.
M: Teaching them to save is important. We opened a savings account when they were young. After birthdays and Christmas, they would go to the branch and deposit their gift money.
W: Oh, I hadn't considered doing that. In our house, we have transparent money boxes for them to put small change in, so they can see their savings grow.
M: When the time is right, I'll start talking to our children about investing and show them how the money saved for their further education has grown.
W: I am always talking to my elder daughter about the importance of saving into a pension. She's just started a part-time job and was thinking of not contributing to her pension. Luckily, I managed to persuade her otherwise.
M: Yes, it's such an important lesson to learn.

groups.title: Section B · 第 2 篇 · 12–15 题
groups.material:
W: Welcome to Books in Review. Our guest today is John Banks, the author of the best selling new book, Rewarding Success.
M: Glad to be here, Jane.
W: Your book has sold 2 million copies, but before we discuss why it's getting so much attention, let's talk about your background. You're an economist and spent two decades teaching at universities?
M: I spent 25 years as a professor, actually. And then, for the last 10 years, I've worked as a political consultant, advising politicians at the national level about problems in our country.
W: You discuss three of those problems in the book, improving public education, reducing our nation's healthcare burden, and increasing personal savings. But your ideas about education are the most controversial.
M: Absolutely. A lot of people think I'm trying to punish students who aren't doing well, when actually my goal is to give all students more incentive to succeed.
W: I'm not sure I agree with you. Your proposal to pay cash rewards to students who get good grades is a particular problem. What about students who don't get good grades? It seems like you're blaming them for not succeeding, when poor performance in school isn't a child's fault.
M: But my proposal is not just to reward students with good grades, but also students who show improvements.
W: Okay, another criticism of the plan is the cash rewards themselves. Where will the money come from?
M: If students do better, we'll spend less on schooling. So, in the end, the rewards will pay for themselves.
W: What about now? How will we fund the rewards in the meantime?
M: Well, by increasing taxes or moving money from other areas of the budget into education.

groups.title: Section C · 第 1 篇 · 16–18 题
groups.material:
I met three different people today, and each time, when I asked, "How are you?" The reply was exactly the same. "I'm busy". Honestly, I hear the same answer from the vast majority of people I meet. So I started to think: "Guess what? Everybody's busy!" I'm busy, you're busy, everybody's busy. So you being busy doesn't make me sympathetic at all. Because "busy" is the state of the world.
So I'm launching a campaign to stop people complaining about being "busy." It may sound harsh, but the truth is, nobody cares. In a busy world, "being busy" doesn't stand out, nor does it mean productive, creative, accomplished, or professional.
Steve Maraboli once said, "When someone tells you they are too 'busy', it's not a reflection of their schedule; it's a reflection of YOUR spot on their schedule." Donna Lynn Hope has also remarked, "Busy doesn't mean better. I've never envied a busy person—the one who likes to point out their busy lives to others."
The reality is, nobody is too busy—it's just about priorities. So the next time someone asks you how you are, maybe respond differently. In my experience, the "I'm busy" response is really covering up the fact that they're not actually accomplishing their real purpose. And "being busy" is the lie they tell themselves about why they can't achieve it.

groups.title: Section C · 第 2 篇 · 19–21 题
groups.material:
More and more people are taking up extreme sports, like snowboarding, skateboarding, mountain biking, and many more. Why are these sports becoming so popular?
One thing that extreme sports do better than perhaps anything else is to help you stop being afraid. It may sound strange to say that their main function is to reduce fear. But after a time, your fear response to other things in life will be dramatically reduced. After all, if you can jump out of a plane or off a bridge, then you can face anything else easily.
When doing extreme sports, you have to become more focused. You'll be pushed to your limits, and if you aren't focused you'll make dangerous mistakes. Learning to be this focused when enjoying extreme sports will help you to be focused at work, keeping you more productive and ultimately more successful.
It's great to stay fit and healthy, but standard exercise routines and sports only work the same muscles repeatedly. With extreme sports, you'll be working entirely different muscles, and that means you get an all-over workout. Extreme sports also burn a lot more calories than other sports. Skateboarding, for example, can burn as many as 500 calories per hour. Basketball burns around 300 in the same time.
When you find that you can overcome the physical or mental challenges involved in extreme sports, you'll feel superhuman and your self-confidence will be at an all-time high.

groups.title: Section C · 第 3 篇 · 22–25 题
groups.material:
Most of us have been in teams or organizations where we've had conflict with the people that we're working with around the ideas or decisions that we're discussing. Conflict is natural. We all bring different life and work experiences to the table. We all have different personality preferences and tendencies. We're not all going to have the same ideas on how to approach policies, programs or problems.
But too often we get caught in this place where conflict is perceived to be negative—something we want to avoid so that we can maintain the harmony of our workplace. This could be because some people want to avoid conflict at all costs, after all they still have to work together. But this kind of artificial harmony isn't the answer.
Productive conflict is a vital part of teams and organizations that want to push forward and do more. Without conflict, we're often stuck in this artificial harmony where people don't express potentially innovative ideas for fear that they may start conflict with others.
But if you're in a place where you have a basis of trust, conflict can be extremely productive. It can lead to increased innovation and greater trust on teams. It may be an uncomfortable process, but good leaders and healthy teams recognize that productive and healthy conflict is an important part of how they function.

questions.prompt: What do we learn about the JetBlue Airlines flight from the news report?
options: It hit a bird shortly after takeoff.
Its crew members went on strike.
It narrowly escaped a plane crash when turning around.
Its captain got slightly injured during the forced landing.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 What do we learn about the JetBlue Airlines flight from the news report? 

 【翻译】 从新闻报道中我们了解到关于捷蓝航空公司航班的什么信息? 
 A)  起飞后不久撞上了一只鸟。 
 B)  机组人员举行了罢工。 
 C)  掉头时险些发生坠机事故。 
 D)  机长在迫降过程中受了轻伤。 

 【答案】 A （细节题） It hit a bird shortly after takeoff. 
 【定位】 P1 A JetBlue Airlines flight from West Palm Beach to New York City was forced to turn around and land Sunday morning after the plane struck a bird. 
 周日上午，一架从西棕榈滩飞往纽约市的捷蓝航空航班在撞上一只鸟之后，被迫调头返航降落。 

 【信号】 新闻首句即事件核心 。答案就在录音第一句 was forced to turn around and land Sunday morning after the plane struck a bird：新闻报道往往开篇一句话就把 "谁、发生了什么、为什么" 交代清楚，这句的 after 引出原因（撞鸟），正是承载答案的核心句。 

 【替换】 after the plane struck a bird ↔ It hit a bird struck 换成 hit 
 was forced to turn around and land Sunday morning ↔ shortly after takeoff 返航即起飞后不久 

 【排除】 B) 未提及 Its crew members went on strike 说机组罢工，录音通篇只字未提任何罢工，返航原因明确是撞鸟，属于无中生有。 
 C) 过度推断 It narrowly escaped a plane crash when turning around 盗用了录音里真出现的 turn around（返航）来制造熟悉感，但录音只说返航降落、明说 No injuries were reported，根本没提 "险些坠机"，是把普通返航夸大成濒临坠机。  借用原文：turned around just minutes after takeoff 

 D) 与原文相反 Its captain got slightly injured during the forced landing 借用了录音真有的 forced to turn around and land（被迫降落）来骗耳朵，但录音紧接着明说 No injuries were reported on the plane——没有任何人受伤，更没说机长受伤，与原文正好相反。  借用原文：No injuries were reported on the plane
questions.spoken_text: What do we learn about the JetBlue Airlines flight from the news report?

questions.prompt: How did the passengers feel when the plane came to a stop, according to Brian Healy?
options: Panic.
Nervous.
Relieved.
Contented.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 How did the passengers feel when the plane came to a stop, according to Brian Healy? 

 【翻译】 根据Brian Healy所说,当飞机停下来时乘客们感觉如何? 
 A)  恐慌。 
 B)  紧张。 
 C)  如释重负。 
 D)  满意。 

 【答案】 C （态度观点题） Relieved. 
 【定位】 P2 "There was total quiet, and then there was relief when the plane came to a stop." 
 "当时一片寂静，随后在飞机停稳的那一刻，大家都松了一口气。" 

 【信号】 题干时间词对准原文 。录音里 there was relief when the plane came to a stop 这句的时间状语 when the plane came to a stop 与题干一字不差，时间点对上，这句就是答案句；情绪词是 relief（松了口气）。 

 【替换】 there was relief ↔ Relieved 名词relief转形容词Relieved 

 【排除】 A) 答非所问 Panic 盗用了录音真说过的 a split second of panic，但那是描述事发瞬间（split second）的情绪，不是题干问的 "飞机停稳时"，时间点错位。  借用原文：a split second of panic 

 B) 答非所问 Nervous 盗用了录音的 this nervous reaction on the plane，但那形容的是事件过程中的紧张反应，同样不是 "飞机停稳时" 的感受，时间点不符。  借用原文：this nervous reaction on the plane 

 D) 未提及 Contented（满足）和正确项 relief 意思相近，是赌你分不清两个正面情绪词，但录音从头到尾只说了 relief，从没出现 "满足" 这层意思，属于无中生有。
questions.spoken_text: How did the passengers feel when the plane came to a stop according to Brian Healy.

questions.prompt: What do we learn about the deadly snake from the news report?
options: He is now kept in a secure area.
He has escaped the zoo once again.
He has been caught a second time.
He finally disappeared six days ago.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 What do we learn about the deadly snake from the news report? 

 【翻译】 从新闻报道中我们对这条致命的蛇了解到什么？ 
 A)  它现在被关在一个安全区域。 
 B)  它再次从动物园逃脱了。 
 C)  它已经第二次被抓住了。 
 D)  它最终在六天前消失了。 

 【答案】 B （细节题） He has escaped the zoo once again. 
 【定位】 P1 A deadly snake, which had finally been tracked down after escaping a zoo, has slipped away for the second time. 
 一条致命的蛇，在逃出动物园后终于被找回，如今又第二次溜走了。 

 【信号】 开篇首句即落点 。新闻的核心事实常压在第一句。这里 has slipped away for the second time（第二次溜走了）就是承载答案的信号句——它点明这条蛇"再次逃跑"这一最新状态。 

 【替换】 has slipped away for the second time ↔ has escaped the zoo once again slip away=escape，second time=once again 

 【排除】 A) 原词陷阱 录音确实念到 placed in a supposedly secure area（被放进所谓安全区域），但紧接着就是 yet again he is out on the loose——它早跑出来了。A 盗用 secure area 这个原词，描述的却是已被推翻的"上一个阶段"状态，不是它"现在"的状况。  借用原文：placed in a supposedly secure area 

 C) 与原文相反 录音里确有 tracked down 和 found（被找到/被抓）以及 second time 的字眼，C 用 caught a second time 把这些原词拼起来。但 second time 在录音里是修饰"逃跑"的（slipped away for the second time），抓只发生过一次。C 把动作方向从"逃"偷换成"抓"，与原文相反。  借用原文：tracked down after escaping a zoo, has slipped away for the second time 

 D) 原词陷阱 录音的 After six days of desperate searching（搜寻了六天）里确有 six days，D 便拿 six days ago 来骗。但六天指的是"工作人员搜寻它花的时长"，不是它"六天前消失"；而且它现在是又跑了、不是"finally disappeared（终于消失）"。数字对得上、事却对不上。  借用原文：After six days of desperate searching
questions.spoken_text: What do we learn about the deadly snake from the news report?

questions.prompt: How have the zoo staff been feeling about the snake?
options: Squeezed.
Threatened.
Disappointed.
Frustrated.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 How have the zoo staff been feeling about the snake? 

 【翻译】 动物园工作人员对这条蛇一直有何感受？ 
 A)  受挤压的。 
 B)  受威胁的。 
 C)  失望的。 
 D)  沮丧的。 

 【答案】 D （态度观点题） Frustrated. 
 【定位】 P2 The snake is a relative newcomer to the zoo but has already been frustrating its staff. 
 这条蛇到动物园不算久，却已经让它的工作人员伤透了脑筋（备受挫败）。 

 【信号】 情绪动词 frustrating 。答案信号就是那个直接表达感受的词 frustrating its staff（让工作人员受挫/懊恼）。态度题的落点往往就是这样一个带感情色彩的形容词或动词，听到它就锁定。 

 【替换】 has already been frustrating its staff ↔ Frustrated 主动 frustrating→被动 frustrated 

 【排除】 A) 原词陷阱 录音里 he squeezed himself out of a gap（蛇把自己挤出缝隙）确有 squeezed，A 就拿这个原词来骗。但 squeezed 讲的是蛇"怎么逃出去的"动作，根本不是工作人员的"感受"，与题目问的 feeling 完全是两码事。  借用原文：he squeezed himself out of a gap 

 B) 未提及 这条蛇虽 deadly（致命），但录音从没说工作人员"感到受威胁"。Threatened 是顺着"毒蛇危险"自行脑补出来的情绪，录音里并无对应的词，属无中生有。 
 C) 偷换概念 Disappointed（失望）与正确的 Frustrated（受挫/懊恼）都是负面情绪、含义相邻，最难切开。但录音明明白白念的是 frustrating，不是 disappointing。C 用一个意思相近却并非原文的情绪词来顶替，差在"不是录音说的那个词"。  借用原文：has already been frustrating its staff
questions.spoken_text: how have the zoo staff been feeling about the snake?

questions.prompt: What do we learn from the news report about the introduction of electric bikes into Jacksonville?
options: It is condemned as a crazy idea.
It is enriching the city's night life.
It is questioned by local residents.
It is giving rise to safety concerns.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 What do we learn from the news report about the introduction of electric bikes into Jacksonville? 

 【翻译】 从新闻报道中我们了解到关于Jacksonville引入电动自行车的哪些信息？ 
 A)  它被谴责为一个疯狂的想法。 
 B)  它正在丰富这座城市的夜生活。 
 C)  它受到当地居民的质疑。 
 D)  它正在引发安全担忧。 

 【答案】 D （细节题） It is giving rise to safety concerns. 
 【定位】 P1 But they're leading to safety concerns, mainly at night when some riders don't follow the rules of the road. 
 但它们正在引发安全担忧，主要发生在夜里，一些骑车人不遵守交通规则的时候。 

 【信号】 转折 But 之后才是真意 。答案藏在转折词后面：第 1 段先说电动车很火 Electric bikes have been the craze，紧接一个 But they're leading to safety concerns。新闻里 But 一转，前面的火爆是铺垫，转折后的安全担忧才是报道真正要讲的落点。 

 【替换】 they're leading to safety concerns ↔ It is giving rise to safety concerns. lead to = give rise to 

 【排除】 A) 原词陷阱 录音说电动车 have been the craze（很火爆、风靡），A 项 condemned as a crazy idea 把 craze 这个原词联想成「crazy／疯狂主意被谴责」。craze（风靡）和 crazy（疯狂）发音相近但意思相反，录音根本没有谴责之意，是听音近词就选的陷阱。  借用原文：Electric bikes have been the craze 

 B) 张冠李戴 enriching the city's night life 听着像呼应录音里夜里、城市等词，但录音第 4 段说的是引进电动车是为了 bring new life into downtown（带来新活力，那是目的／初衷），并没说它正在丰富夜生活。把第 4 段的目的安到第 5 题的现状评价上，张冠李戴。  借用原文：bring new life into downtown 

 C) 未提及 questioned by local residents 里的「被本地居民质疑」在录音里找不到落点：报道讲的是 safety concerns（安全担忧），并没有出现 local residents 质疑这一方。属于无中生有。
questions.spoken_text: what do we learn from the news report about the introduction of electric bikes into Jacksonville

questions.prompt: What are electric bike riders supposed to do?
options: Avoid entering one-way streets.
Ensure the safety of pedestrians.
Follow all the traffic rules drivers do.
Give way to automobiles at all times.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 What are electric bike riders supposed to do? 

 【翻译】 电动自行车骑行者应该做什么？ 
 A)  避免进入单行道。 
 B)  确保行人的安全。 
 C)  遵守驾驶员遵守的所有交通规则。 
 D)  任何时候都给机动车让行。 

 【答案】 C （细节题） Follow all the traffic rules drivers do. 
 【定位】 P3 Electric bike riders have to follow all the same rules as you would if you were in an automobile. 
 电动车骑车人必须遵守和你开汽车时一样的全部规则。 

 【信号】 义务句 have to 即落点 。第 3 段 have to follow all the same rules 里的 have to（必须）是明确的义务标志。预读时就定了「听 have to／must」，这句一出现就是答案句。 

 【替换】 follow all the same rules as you would if you were in an automobile ↔ Follow all the traffic rules drivers do. in an automobile = drivers do 

 【排除】 A) 原词陷阱 Avoid entering one-way streets 盗用了录音 one-way streets 这个原词，但录音说的是「不要在单行道上逆行（traveling in the opposite direction）」，不是「避免进入单行道」。它只截取了规则里的一个例子并改了意思，答非所问——题目问的是总要求，不是某一条细则。  借用原文：traveling in the opposite direction of traffic on one-way streets 

 B) 张冠李戴 Ensure the safety of pedestrians 里的 pedestrians 借自第 2 段 pedestrian paths。但录音从没要求骑车人「保证行人安全」；第 4 段只说骑车人和司机都要 paying attention（注意安全）。把注意夸成保证行人安全，且 pedestrian 一词出处也不对，张冠李戴。  借用原文：on pedestrian paths 

 D) 原词陷阱 Give way to automobiles at all times 借了录音的 automobile 一词，但录音说骑车人要遵守「和开汽车一样的规则」，是平等守规，绝没有「随时给汽车让路」的意思。at all times（任何时候）是绝对化的无中生有。  借用原文：as you would if you were in an automobile
questions.spoken_text: What are electric bike riders supposed to do?

questions.prompt: Why did City Council member Anna Cumber advocate the introduction of electric bikes into Jacksonville?
options: To ease the city's busy traffic.
To bring new life into the city.
To add a new means of transport.
To reduce the city's air pollution.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 Why did City Council member Anna Cumber advocate the introduction of electric bikes into Jacksonville? 

 【翻译】 为什么市议会成员Anna Cumber倡导在Jacksonville引入电动自行车？ 
 A)  为了缓解城市的繁忙交通。 
 B)  为了给城市带来新的活力。 
 C)  为了增加一种新的交通方式。 
 D)  为了减少城市的空气污染。 

 【答案】 B （目的题） To bring new life into the city. 
 【定位】 P4 City Council Member Anna Cumber was instrumental in introducing the electric bikes to Jacksonville as a way to bring new life into downtown. 
 市议会议员 Anna Cumber 在把电动车引进杰克逊维尔一事上起了关键作用，目的是给市中心带来新的活力。 

 【信号】 目的状语 as a way to 。第 4 段 as a way to bring new life into downtown 里的 as a way to（作为……的一种方式）就是明确的目的标志，它后面接的就是 Anna Cumber 引进电动车的初衷。预读已锁定听目的结构，这句正中。 

 【替换】 as a way to bring new life into downtown ↔ To bring new life into the city. downtown = the city 

 【排除】 A) 未提及 To ease the city's busy traffic 听着合理，但录音里 Anna Cumber 引进电动车的目的只说了 bring new life into downtown，从没提缓解繁忙交通。属无中生有的合理化推断。 
 C) 过度推断 To add a new means of transport 看似没错——电动车确实是新交通工具，但录音点明的目的是带来新活力，不是增加一种交通方式。这是顺着常识多推一步、偏离原文所说目的。 
 D) 未提及 To reduce the city's air pollution 引入「空气污染」这个全新概念，录音通篇没出现 pollution 或环保相关内容。属彻底的无中生有。

questions.prompt: What should we do with the topic of money, according to the woman?
options: Take it seriously.
Discuss it regularly.
Make it sound scary.
Talk about it openly.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 What should we do with the topic of money, according to the woman? 

 【翻译】 根据这位女士的说法,我们应该如何对待金钱这个话题? 
 A)  认真对待它。 
 B)  定期讨论它。 
 C)  让它听起来很可怕。 
 D)  公开谈论它。 

 【答案】 B （细节题） Discuss it regularly. 
 【定位】 P2 You should make money a regular topic of discussion. 
 你应该让钱成为一个经常讨论的话题。 

 【信号】 应答方的 should 建议句 。男士问"最好怎么教孩子理财"，女士开口第一句就是 You should make money a regular topic of discussion，should 是明确的建议信号，被问者的应答正是答案落点。 

 【替换】 a regular topic of discussion ↔ Discuss it regularly 名词短语改写成动词 

 【排除】 A) 未提及 Take it seriously.（认真对待）听起来很顺理成章，但女士没说要"认真严肃对待"，反而强调要让它不吓人、变本能，属凭常识脑补、原文未提。 
 C) 与原文相反 录音里女士说要让钱"不是个吓人的话题" rather than a scary subject，Make it sound scary. 盗用了原词 scary 却把意思反了过来，正是"听到原词就想选"的陷阱。  借用原文：rather than a scary subject 

 D) 张冠李戴 Talk about it openly. 对应的 openly 来自男士的话 we talk openly about things，是男士说的，而题目问的是 according to the woman（女士），把男士的话安到女士头上，属张冠李戴。  借用原文：we talk openly about things

questions.prompt: How does the woman say money can be made real for children?
options: By shopping around for the best deals.
By making abstract sums relevant.
By citing concrete examples.
By visiting discount stores.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 How does the woman say money can be made real for children? 

 【翻译】 这位女士说如何能让金钱对孩子们变得真实? 
 A)  通过货比三家寻找最优惠的价格。 
 B)  通过让抽象的金额变得相关。 
 C)  通过引用具体的例子。 
 D)  通过参观折扣商店。 

 【答案】 C （细节题） By citing concrete examples. 
 【定位】 P4 It's also essential to make money real for children through practical examples. Working out how much we save using discount pizza coupons, for example, is much more relevant than abstract sums. 
 通过实际的例子让钱对孩子变得真实也很重要。比如算一算我们用披萨折扣券省了多少钱，这比抽象的算数有意义得多。 

 【信号】 for example 引出具体做法 。女士说要 through practical examples 并紧接 for example 举出披萨折扣券的例子，practical examples 加 for example 正是"用具体例子"的方式信号，承载 How 的答案。 

 【替换】 through practical examples ↔ By citing concrete examples 同义词替换 

 【排除】 A) 原词陷阱 By shopping around for the best deals. 里 shopping around for the best deals 是男士在 how to shop around for the best deals 里说的别的话题，且非"让钱变真实"的方法，原词照搬却答非所问。  借用原文：how to shop around for the best deals 

 B) 与原文相反 录音说具体例子"比抽象算数有意义得多" much more relevant than abstract sums，abstract sums 是被否定、被比下去的一方；By making abstract sums relevant. 盗用这两个词反过来说"让抽象算数变得相关"，与原文相反。  借用原文：much more relevant than abstract sums 

 D) 偷换概念 By visiting discount stores. 里 discount 来自录音的 discount pizza coupons（折扣券），但原文是"用折扣券"不是"逛折扣店"，盗一个 discount 把概念偷换了。  借用原文：discount pizza coupons

questions.prompt: What is the common practice between the man and the woman?
options: Paying their kids to help with housework.
Setting kids a good example by sharing chores.
Giving kids pocket money according to their needs.
Urging kids to deposit some of their gift money.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 What is the common practice between the man and the woman? 

 【翻译】 这位男士和这位女士之间的共同做法是什么? 
 A)  付钱给孩子们帮忙做家务。 
 B)  通过分担家务给孩子们树立好榜样。 
 C)  根据孩子们的需要给他们零花钱。 
 D)  督促孩子们存一些压岁钱。 

 【答案】 A （细节题） Paying their kids to help with housework. 
 【定位】 P6 M: We also give our kids pocket money, and the amount they get is linked to chores, such as putting the bins out and emptying the dishwasher. W: We do that too, and it's paid according to their age. 
 男：我们也给孩子零花钱，金额跟做家务挂钩，比如倒垃圾、清空洗碗机。女：我们也这么做，而且是按年龄发的。 

 【信号】 We do that too 的附和 。男士说零花钱"跟做家务挂钩" the amount they get is linked to chores，女士紧接 We do that too（我们也这么做），这句附和正是"共同做法"的信号，把男士那件事确认为两人共有。 

 【替换】 pocket money, and the amount they get is linked to chores ↔ Paying their kids to help with housework 挂钩家务即按家务付钱 
 We do that too ↔ 10A 附和坐实共同点 

 【排除】 B) 未提及 Setting kids a good example by sharing chores.（以分担家务给孩子做榜样）听着合理，但录音说的是"让孩子做家务换零花钱"，不是大人分担家务做榜样，原文并无此意。 
 C) 原词陷阱 Giving kids pocket money according to their needs. 照搬原词 pocket money，但加的条件是 according to their needs（按需要），录音里是"按家务"和"按年龄" it's paid according to their age，条件被偷换。  借用原文：it's paid according to their age 

 D) 张冠李戴 Urging kids to deposit some of their gift money. 里 deposit、gift money 出自男士单方面的 they would go to the branch and deposit their gift money，女士回应说"我没考虑过这么做"，并非两人共同做法。  借用原文：they would go to the branch and deposit their gift money

questions.prompt: What is the woman always talking about to her elder daughter?
options: The importance of cutting down family expenses.
The need to learn important lessons from her elders.
The delight in seeing their savings grow.
The necessity of saving into a pension.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 What is the woman always talking about to her elder daughter? 

 【翻译】 这位女士总是和她的大女儿谈论什么? 
 A)  削减家庭开支的重要性。 
 B)  需要向长辈学习重要的经验教训。 
 C)  看到他们的储蓄增长的喜悦。 
 D)  向养老金储蓄的必要性。 

 【答案】 D （细节题） The necessity of saving into a pension. 
 【定位】 P10 W: I am always talking to my elder daughter about the importance of saving into a pension. 
 女：我总是跟我大女儿讲存钱进养老金的重要性。 

 【信号】 always + importance 强调 。女士说 I am always talking to my elder daughter about the importance of saving into a pension，always 与 importance 双重强调，且对象 elder daughter 与题干完全一致，这句即答案落点。 

 【替换】 the importance of saving into a pension ↔ The necessity of saving into a pension importance 换成 necessity 

 【排除】 A) 未提及 The importance of cutting down family expenses.（削减家庭开支的重要性）虽与省钱沾边，但录音里女士对女儿谈的是"存养老金"，从未谈"削减家庭开支"，属无中生有。 
 B) 原词陷阱 The need to learn important lessons from her elders. 盗用了男士末句的 it's such an important lesson to learn 与选项 11 里 elder daughter 的 elder，但 from her elders（向长辈学）方向反了，女士是"对女儿讲"不是"向长辈学"。  借用原文：it's such an important lesson to learn 

 C) 张冠李戴 The delight in seeing their savings grow. 里 see savings grow 来自女士前面讲存钱罐的 so they can see their savings grow，那是对小孩子说的，不是对大女儿谈的内容，被错接到本题。  借用原文：so they can see their savings grow

questions.prompt: What do we learn about the man?
options: He is a successful businessman.
He reviews books on political affairs.
He has published a new bestseller.
He has worked in several banks.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 What do we learn about the man? 

 【翻译】 关于这位男士我们了解到什么? 
 A)  他是一位成功的商人。 
 B)  他评论政治事务方面的书籍。 
 C)  他出版了一本新的畅销书。 
 D)  他曾在几家银行工作过。 

 【答案】 C （细节题） He has published a new bestseller. 
 【定位】 P1 Our guest today is John Banks, the author of the best selling new book, Rewarding Success. 
 今天的嘉宾是约翰·班克斯，畅销新书《奖励成功》的作者。 

 【信号】 主持人开场介绍嘉宾 。信号是访谈开场的身份介绍句 Our guest today is John Banks, the author of the best selling new book——主持人介绍嘉宾时点出的身份，正是人物题答案最常藏身处。 

 【替换】 the author of the best selling new book ↔ He has published a new bestseller. "畅销书作者"="出版了畅销书" 

 【排除】 A) 未提及 录音说他是作者、教授、政治顾问，从没说他是商人；He is a successful businessman. 属凭"成功"二字（书名 Rewarding Success）联想出来的误判，文中无据。 
 B) 张冠李戴 He reviews books on political affairs. 盗用了开场 Books in Review（节目名"书评"）和 author of the book 里的 book 字样，骗"听到 book/review 就选"。但评书的是主持人，他是被采访的作者，身份张冠李戴。  借用原文：Welcome to Books in Review 

 D) 原词陷阱 He has worked in several banks. 借的是嘉宾姓 John Banks 里的 Banks（人名）和后文谈经济、税收的氛围，骗人误以为他在银行工作过。实际他干的是 worked as a political consultant，与银行无关。  借用原文：John Banks

questions.prompt: What does the woman say is the most controversial?
options: The man's ideas about education.
The man's academic background.
The man's attempts at drawing public attention.
The man's proposals to solve economic problems.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 What does the woman say is the most controversial? 

 【翻译】 女士说最具争议的是什么? 
 A)  这位男士关于教育的观点。 
 B)  这位男士的学术背景。 
 C)  这位男士吸引公众关注的尝试。 
 D)  这位男士解决经济问题的提案。 

 【答案】 A （细节题） The man's ideas about education. 
 【定位】 P5 You discuss three of those problems in the book, improving public education, reducing our nation's healthcare burden, and increasing personal savings. But your ideas about education are the most controversial. 
 你在书里谈了其中三个问题：改善公共教育、减轻国家医疗负担、增加个人储蓄。但你关于教育的主张最具争议。 

 【信号】 转折 But + 最高级 the most controversial 。信号是女方话里的转折加最高级 But your ideas about education are the most controversial.——But 之后才是她真正想强调的落点，the most controversial 直接点名争议所在。 

 【替换】 your ideas about education are the most controversial ↔ The man's ideas about education. 近乎原句，只换 your→The man's 

 【排除】 B) 原词陷阱 The man's academic background. 盗用了前文 let's talk about your background 里的 background。但谈背景是 But 之前的铺垫闲聊，女方明确说"最有争议"的是教育主张，不是背景。  借用原文：let's talk about your background 

 C) 偷换概念 The man's attempts at drawing public attention. 借了前文 why it's getting so much attention 里的 attention。原文 attention 指的是"书为何受关注"，并非说他"刻意博关注"，是把客观受关注偷换成主观博眼球。  借用原文：why it's getting so much attention 

 D) 偷换概念 The man's proposals to solve economic problems. 沾了全书谈经济问题的大背景。但女方点名最具争议的是 education（教育）这一具体领域，不是笼统的"经济提案"，范围对不上。  借用原文：problems in our country

questions.prompt: What does the man say is his real goal?
options: To reduce students' financial burden.
To motivate all students to be successful.
To give students incentive to excel in economics.
To provide remedies for students' poor performance.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 What does the man say is his real goal? 

 【翻译】 男士说他的真正目标是什么? 
 A)  减轻学生的经济负担。 
 B)  激励所有学生取得成功。 
 C)  给予学生在经济学方面出类拔萃的动力。 
 D)  为学生的不良表现提供补救措施。 

 【答案】 B （细节题） To motivate all students to be successful. 
 【定位】 P6 A lot of people think I'm trying to punish students who aren't doing well, when actually my goal is to give all students more incentive to succeed. 
 很多人以为我想惩罚成绩不好的学生，其实我的目标是给所有学生更多动力去取得成功。 

 【信号】 actually + my goal is 的澄清句 。信号是他亲口纠正误解的句子 when actually my goal is to give all students more incentive to succeed——actually 推翻前面"人们以为"的误解，my goal is 直接交代真实目的，正是 real goal 题的答案落点。 

 【替换】 to give all students more incentive to succeed ↔ To motivate all students to be successful. give incentive=motivate，succeed=be successful 

 【排除】 A) 未提及 To reduce students' financial burden. 谈减轻经济负担，但他在第 6 段说的目的是"给学生动力"，与减负无关；减负是另一个层面的话题，文中没把它当作他的目标。 
 C) 原词陷阱 To give students incentive to excel in economics. 几乎照搬原话 give … incentive，却把 all students to succeed 偷偷缩成 excel in economics（在经济学上拔尖）。他要激励的是所有学生取得成功，不限于经济这一科。  借用原文：to give all students more incentive to succeed 

 D) 与原文相反 To provide remedies for students' poor performance. 借了女方后文 poor performance in school 的原词，听着像"针对差生补救"。但他的目的恰恰不是只盯差生——这正是他要澄清反对的"惩罚差生"那层误解的变体。  借用原文：poor performance in school isn't a child's fault

questions.prompt: What will be one option for funding the proposed rewards according to the man?
options: Improving school budgeting.
Increasing tuition fees.
Seeking donations.
Raising taxes.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 What will be one option for funding the proposed rewards according to the man? 

 【翻译】 根据男士所说,为拟议的奖励提供资金的一个选择是什么? 
 A)  改善学校预算。 
 B)  提高学费。 
 C)  寻求捐赠。 
 D)  提高税收。 

 【答案】 D （细节题） Raising taxes. 
 【定位】 P12 Well, by increasing taxes or moving money from other areas of the budget into education. 
 嗯，靠加税，或者把预算中其他领域的钱挪到教育上来。 

 【信号】 对被问者"钱怎么出"的直接应答 。信号是被问方对女方提问 How will we fund the rewards in the meantime? 的直接应答 by increasing taxes or moving money from other areas——对话题里问题落在哪、答案就在被问者那句应答里。 

 【替换】 by increasing taxes ↔ Raising taxes. increase taxes=raise taxes 

 【排除】 A) 原词陷阱 Improving school budgeting. 盗用了原话 moving money from other areas of the budget 里的 budget。但他说的是"把预算里别处的钱挪进教育"，不是"改善学校的预算编制"，做法被偷换。  借用原文：moving money from other areas of the budget into education 

 B) 未提及 Increasing tuition fees. 与正确项 Raising taxes. 共用 increase/raise 结构、都谈"加钱"，极易混。但他全程没提涨学费，只说加税和挪预算，tuition 是凭"学校、学生"话题脑补的。 
 C) 未提及 Seeking donations. 即募集捐款，录音里他只给了加税和挪预算两条路，从没提过募捐，属凭"筹钱"话题硬补的选项。

questions.prompt: Why is the speaker launching a campaign?
options: To show his sympathy towards people always being busy.
To prevent people from complaining about being "busy".
To call on busy people to take care of themselves.
To help busy people to sort out their priorities.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 Why is the speaker launching a campaign? 

 【翻译】 说话者为什么发起一项运动？ 
 A)  表达他对总是忙碌的人们的同情。 
 B)  阻止人们抱怨自己很"忙"。 
 C)  呼吁忙碌的人们照顾好自己。 
 D)  帮助忙碌的人们理清他们的优先事项。 

 【答案】 B （目的题） To prevent people from complaining about being "busy". 
 【定位】 P2 So I'm launching a campaign to stop people complaining about being "busy." 
 所以我要发起一场运动，让大家别再抱怨『忙』了。 

 【信号】 to 引出意图，紧跟在 campaign 后 。答案句里 campaign 后面紧跟一个 to stop people complaining，这个不定式直接交代了发起运动的目的——听到 launching a campaign to… 时，to 后面那一截就是答案落点，这是目的题最典型的信号。 

 【替换】 to stop people complaining about being "busy." ↔ To prevent people from complaining about being "busy". stop = prevent，近义替换 

 【排除】 A) 原词陷阱 A 项 To show his sympathy towards people always being busy. 利用了原文 you being busy doesn't make me sympathetic at all 里的 sympathetic 一词，但原话是『一点也不让我同情』，说话人恰恰是不同情，A 把否定听成了肯定、方向反了。  借用原文：you being busy doesn't make me sympathetic at all 

 C) 未提及 C 项 To call on busy people to take care of themselves. 说发起运动是为了呼吁忙人照顾好自己，但全文从未提到 take care of themselves，说话人发起运动是为了让人别再抱怨忙，而非关心忙人的健康，属凭常识臆造。 
 D) 原词陷阱 D 项 To help busy people to sort out their priorities. 借了原文 it's just about priorities 里的 priorities 一词，但那句是在第四段解释『没人真的太忙、只是优先级问题』，并不是发起运动的目的；D 把后文一个无关概念词搬来充当发起动机，张冠李戴。  借用原文：nobody is too busy—it's just about priorities
questions.spoken_text: Why is the speaker launching a campaign?

questions.prompt: What does the speaker advise us to do next time someone asks how we are?
options: Avoid saying we are busy.
Reflect on their true purpose.
Describe our schedule in detail.
Respond as most busy people do.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 What does the speaker advise us to do next time someone asks how we are? 

 【翻译】 当下次有人问我们怎么样时，说话者建议我们做什么？ 
 A)  避免说我们很忙。 
 B)  反思他们的真实目的。 
 C)  详细描述我们的日程安排。 
 D)  像大多数忙碌的人那样回应。 

 【答案】 A （细节题） Avoid saying we are busy. 
 【定位】 P4 So the next time someone asks you how you are, maybe respond differently. 
 所以下次有人问你『最近怎么样』，也许可以换个方式回答。 

 【信号】 next time + maybe，建议信号 。答案句以 So the next time someone asks you how you are 起头、接 maybe respond differently，next time 与建议词 maybe 连用，正是说话人给建议的标志句——听到 maybe / you should / next time 一类软建议词，后面那句就是建议内容。 

 【替换】 respond differently ↔ Avoid saying we are busy. differently 的具体所指 = 别再说忙 

 【排除】 B) 原词陷阱 B 项 Reflect on their true purpose. 借了原文反复出现的 purpose（their real purpose）一词，但说话人在第四段讲 real purpose 是在解释『忙是借口』，并没有建议我们『去反思真正目的』；B 把别处的概念词搬来当本题建议，答非所问。  借用原文：they're not actually accomplishing their real purpose 

 C) 原词陷阱 C 项 Describe our schedule in detail. 用了原文出现过的 schedule（YOUR spot on their schedule），但说话人从没建议我们详细描述自己的日程，反而是在反对把『忙』挂嘴边；C 借 schedule 一词编了个原文没给的建议。  借用原文：it's a reflection of YOUR spot on their schedule 

 D) 与原文相反 D 项 Respond as most busy people do. 说『像多数忙人那样回答』，但原文恰恰让你 respond differently（换个方式、不要照旧），D 取了与建议完全相反的方向，正话反说。  借用原文：maybe respond differently
questions.spoken_text: What does the speaker advise us to do? Next time someone asks us how we are.

questions.prompt: Why do many people make the "I'm busy" response according to the speaker?
options: To show their achievements resulted from great efforts.
To prove they stand out as accomplished professionals.
To cover up their failure to achieve some purpose.
To tell others a complete lie about their inability.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 Why do many people make the "I'm busy" response according to the speaker? 

 【翻译】 根据说话者的说法，为什么许多人会做出"我很忙"的回应？ 
 A)  展示他们通过巨大努力取得的成就。 
 B)  证明他们作为有成就的专业人士脱颖而出。 
 C)  掩盖他们未能实现某个目标的事实。 
 D)  向他人彻底撒谎说自己没有能力。 

 【答案】 C （细节题） To cover up their failure to achieve some purpose. 
 【定位】 P4 In my experience, the "I'm busy" response is really covering up the fact that they're not actually accomplishing their real purpose. 
 以我的经验，『我很忙』这种回答其实是在掩盖一个事实——他们并没有真正完成自己真正的目标。 

 【信号】 really + covering up，点出真实原因 。答案句里 is really covering up the fact 的 really（其实/真正）是揭示真相的强调信号，covering up（掩盖）直接说出动机——听到 really / actually / the truth is 这类点真相的词，后面就是说话人要你听到的真实原因。 

 【替换】 covering up the fact that they're not actually accomplishing their real purpose ↔ To cover up their failure to achieve some purpose. 没做成 = failure，概念升级 

 【排除】 A) 原词陷阱 A 项 To show their achievements resulted from great efforts. 用了与原文 accomplished 同根的 achievements，但原文 "being busy" doesn't…mean…accomplished 明说忙并不等于有成就，说话人是在否定『忙=有成就』，A 却说人们这么答是为了炫耀成就，方向反了。  借用原文："being busy" doesn't stand out, nor does it mean productive, creative, accomplished, or professional 

 B) 原词陷阱 B 项 To prove they stand out as accomplished professionals. 同时搬了原文 stand out、accomplished、professional 三个原词，迷惑性很强，但原文那句是说『忙并不让人显得突出、也不代表专业』，是否定；B 反过来说人们答忙是为了证明自己是杰出专业人士，与原意相反、也不是题目问的真实动机。  借用原文："being busy" doesn't stand out, nor does it mean productive, creative, accomplished, or professional 

 D) 原词陷阱 D 项 To tell others a complete lie about their inability. 借了原文 the lie they tell themselves 的 lie，但原文说的是『他们对自己撒的谎』、且没有 complete（彻底）这种程度，D 改成『对别人说彻底的谎、关于自己的无能』，对象（自己→别人）和程度（a lie→a complete lie）都被篡改、过度夸大。  借用原文："being busy" is the lie they tell themselves about why they can't achieve it
questions.spoken_text: Why do many people make the I'm busy response, according to the speaker?

questions.prompt: What may sound strange to say about extreme sports?
options: They will help one reduce fear
They should become so popular.
They will be less challenging after a time.
They should cover so many different types.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 What may sound strange to say about extreme sports? 

 【翻译】 关于极限运动，说什么可能听起来很奇怪? 
 A)  它们会帮助人减少恐惧 
 B)  它们应该变得如此流行。 
 C)  一段时间后它们的挑战性会降低。 
 D)  它们应该涵盖如此多不同的类型。 

 【答案】 A （细节题） They will help one reduce fear 
 【定位】 P2 It may sound strange to say that their main function is to reduce fear. 
 要说极限运动的主要作用是减少恐惧，这听起来也许有点奇怪。 

 【信号】 题干原话 sound strange 在原文回响 。原文 It may sound strange to say that their main function is to reduce fear 把题干里的 may sound strange to say 几乎原样念出，这种"题干措辞在原文重现"是最强定位信号，紧跟其后的 to reduce fear 即答案内容。 

 【替换】 their main function is to reduce fear ↔ They will help one reduce fear main function = will help，reduce fear 原义保留 

 【排除】 B) 原词陷阱 第1段确实念到 Why are these sports becoming so popular?，They should become so popular 把 popular 原词搬来；但"流行"是全文引子，并非那句"听起来奇怪"的说法，属听到原词就想选的原词陷阱。  借用原文：Why are these sports becoming so popular? 

 C) 未提及 They will be less challenging after a time 听起来"奇怪"但录音从未说极限运动会"变得不那么有挑战"；它蹭了第2段 after a time 这个时间词，却把内容编造成"难度下降"，属未提及。  借用原文：after a time, your fear response to other things in life will be dramatically reduced 

 D) 张冠李戴 第1段列举 snowboarding, skateboarding, mountain biking, and many more，They should cover so many different types 借此说"涵盖很多类型"；但这是开篇举例，不是题干所指那句"听起来奇怪"的话，张冠李戴。  借用原文：snowboarding, skateboarding, mountain biking, and many more
questions.spoken_text: What may sound strange to say about extreme sports?

questions.prompt: Why should one be highly focused when doing extreme sports?
options: To break one's ultimate limits.
To stop being extremely afraid.
To avoid dangerous mistakes.
To enjoy the sports to the full.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 Why should one be highly focused when doing extreme sports? 

 【翻译】 为什么在做极限运动时应该高度专注? 
 A)  为了突破个人的极限 
 B)  为了停止极度恐惧 
 C)  为了避免危险的错误 
 D)  为了充分享受这些运动 

 【答案】 C （细节题） To avoid dangerous mistakes. 
 【定位】 P3 You'll be pushed to your limits, and if you aren't focused you'll make dangerous mistakes. 
 你会被逼到极限，如果不专注，就会犯危险的错误。 

 【信号】 if 引出的因果条件句 。if you aren't focused you'll make dangerous mistakes 是个 if 条件句："不专注→犯危险错误"，反过来即"专注是为了避免危险错误"。if…you'll… 的因果结构就是原因题的答案信号。 

 【替换】 if you aren't focused you'll make dangerous mistakes ↔ To avoid dangerous mistakes 肯否转换：不专注就犯错 = 专注为避免犯错 

 【排除】 A) 原词陷阱 原文 You'll be pushed to your limits 念到 limits，To break one's ultimate limits 抢用 limits 制造"听到就选"；但原文是"你会被逼到极限"，并非"专注是为了突破极限"，属原词陷阱。  借用原文：You'll be pushed to your limits 

 B) 张冠李戴 To stop being extremely afraid 对应的是第2段"减少恐惧"的内容，与第3段"为什么要专注"无关；把别段的好处安到本题，张冠李戴。  借用原文：their main function is to reduce fear 

 D) 未提及 To enjoy the sports to the full 听着合理，但录音从没说"专注是为了把运动玩到尽兴"；它无原文出处，是凭常识编出来的，属未提及。

questions.prompt: How can extreme sports benefit us more than standard exercise routines and sports?
options: By allowing our motivation to be at an all-time high.
By stopping us hurting the same muscles repeatedly.
By burning as many as 300 calories per hour.
By enabling us to get an all-over workout.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 How can extreme sports benefit us more than standard exercise routines and sports? 

 【翻译】 极限运动如何比标准锻炼常规和运动更有益? 
 A)  通过让我们的动力达到空前的高度 
 B)  通过阻止我们反复伤害相同的肌肉 
 C)  通过每小时燃烧多达300卡路里 
 D)  通过使我们能够得到全身锻炼 

 【答案】 D （细节题） By enabling us to get an all-over workout. 
 【定位】 P4 With extreme sports, you'll be working entirely different muscles, and that means you get an all-over workout. 
 做极限运动时，你会动用到完全不同的肌肉，这意味着你能得到全身锻炼。 

 【信号】 对比 + that means 引出结论 。前句 standard exercise routines and sports only work the same muscles repeatedly 与本句"动用完全不同肌肉"形成对比，that means you get an all-over workout 用 that means 把结论点出——"对比 + that means 的结论"就是答案信号。 

 【替换】 that means you get an all-over workout ↔ By enabling us to get an all-over workout that means = By enabling us to，all-over workout 原义保留 

 【排除】 A) 原词陷阱 By allowing our motivation to be at an all-time high 盗用第5段 your self-confidence will be at an all-time high 的 all-time high；但原文说的是"自信"达到最高、且与"比常规运动好在哪"无关，且把 self-confidence 偷换成 motivation，原词陷阱兼偷换概念。  借用原文：your self-confidence will be at an all-time high 

 B) 与原文相反 原文说常规运动 only work the same muscles repeatedly（反复练同一块肌肉，是它的不足）；By stopping us hurting the same muscles repeatedly 盗用 same muscles repeatedly，却把它说成极限运动的益处方式，与原文指向相反。  借用原文：only work the same muscles repeatedly 

 C) 原词陷阱 原文 Basketball burns around 300 in the same time，300 是篮球的消耗；极限运动（滑板）是 can burn as many as 500 calories per hour。By burning as many as 300 calories per hour 故意配错数字，是典型数字陷阱。  借用原文：Basketball burns around 300 in the same time

questions.prompt: What does the passage say about conflict in organizations?
options: It is natural.
It is instrumental.
It is personal.
It is vital.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 What does the passage say about conflict in organizations? 

 【翻译】 文章关于组织中的冲突说了什么? 
 A)  这是自然的。 
 B)  这是有益的。 
 C)  这是针对个人的。 
 D)  这是至关重要的。 

 【答案】 A （细节题） It is natural. 
 【定位】 P1 Conflict is natural. We all bring different life and work experiences to the table. 
 冲突是自然的。我们每个人都把各自不同的生活和工作经历带到一起来。 

 【信号】 is + 形容词的直接定性 。答案信号是一句最直白的判断句 Conflict is natural.——主语正是题问的 conflict，紧跟 is + 形容词给它定性，这种'X is + 形容词'的下定义句就是定性题的落点。 

 【替换】 Conflict is natural. ↔ It is natural. 代词替换+原词保留 

 【排除】 B) 未提及 It is instrumental.（起工具/促进作用的）原文从未用来形容冲突，是凭空安上的形容词，与定性句 Conflict is natural. 不符。 
 C) 原词陷阱 原文后文确实提到 We all have different personality preferences and tendencies.，It is personal. 盗用了 personality 这个原词，让人觉得'听到了'。但那句是在解释冲突为何自然，并非给冲突定性为'个人的'，属答非所问。  借用原文：We all have different personality preferences and tendencies. 

 D) 原词陷阱 It is vital. 盗用的是第 3 段 Productive conflict is a vital part of teams and organizations 里的 vital，但那是形容'有益的冲突 productive conflict'，而本题问的是冲突本身的性质，原文这里给的定性是 natural，不是 vital。  借用原文：Productive conflict is a vital part of teams and organizations
questions.spoken_text: What does the passage say about conflict in organizations?

questions.prompt: Why do some people want to avoid conflict at all costs?
options: To guard against being perceived negatively.
To prevent themselves from being isolated.
To conceal personality preferences.
To maintain workplace harmony.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 Why do some people want to avoid conflict at all costs? 

 【翻译】 为什么有些人想不惜一切代价避免冲突? 
 A)  防止被负面看待。 
 B)  防止自己被孤立。 
 C)  隐藏个性偏好。 
 D)  维护工作场所和谐。 

 【答案】 D （细节题） To maintain workplace harmony. 
 【定位】 P2 But too often we get caught in this place where conflict is perceived to be negative—something we want to avoid so that we can maintain the harmony of our workplace. 
 但我们常常陷入这样一种境地：冲突被视为负面的东西——一种我们想要回避的东西，以便能维持工作场所的和谐。 

 【信号】 so that 引出目的 。答案信号是表目的的连接词 so that：something we want to avoid so that we can maintain the harmony of our workplace，so that 之后正是'回避冲突'的目的，这就是 Why 题要的落点。 

 【替换】 so that we can maintain the harmony of our workplace ↔ To maintain workplace harmony. 语序压缩+同词复现 

 【排除】 A) 原词陷阱 To guard against being perceived negatively. 盗用了原文 conflict is perceived to be negative 里的 perceived/negative，听起来很耳熟。但原文那句是说'冲突被视为负面'，是回避的背景，不是人们回避冲突所追求的目的，属答非所问。  借用原文：conflict is perceived to be negative 

 B) 未提及 To prevent themselves from being isolated.（防止自己被孤立）原文从未提到'被孤立'，是凭空添加的目的，与 so that 后的'维持和谐'无关。 
 C) 原词陷阱 To conceal personality preferences. 盗用第 1 段 We all have different personality preferences and tendencies. 里的 personality preferences，但那是讲冲突为何自然，跟'回避冲突的目的'毫不相干，且原文没有'隐藏 conceal'之意。  借用原文：We all have different personality preferences and tendencies.
questions.spoken_text: Why do some people want to avoid conflict at all costs?

questions.prompt: Why is productive conflict important for teams and organizations?
options: It helps to enhance team spirit.
It stimulates innovative ideas.
It helps to resolve problems.
It facilitates policy-making.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 Why is productive conflict important for teams and organizations? 

 【翻译】 为什么建设性冲突对团队和组织很重要? 
 A)  它有助于增强团队精神。 
 B)  它激发创新想法。 
 C)  它有助于解决问题。 
 D)  它促进政策制定。 

 【答案】 B （细节题） It stimulates innovative ideas. 
 【定位】 P3 Without conflict, we're often stuck in this artificial harmony where people don't express potentially innovative ideas for fear that they may start conflict with others. 
 没有冲突，我们往往困在这种虚假的和谐里，人们由于害怕会与他人引发冲突，而不去表达那些可能很有创新性的想法。 

 【信号】 Without...反面论证 。答案信号是 Without conflict 引出的反面假设：没有冲突，人们就不敢说出 potentially innovative ideas。反过来即说明'有益的冲突'的价值就在于能让创新想法被表达出来，这是从反面点出作用的落点。 

 【替换】 people don't express potentially innovative ideas ↔ It stimulates innovative ideas. 否定反推+同词保留 

 【排除】 A) 原词陷阱 It helps to enhance team spirit. 借了原文反复出现的 team(s)，让人一听 team 就想选。但原文说冲突带来的是 innovation 与 trust，从未说它增强'团队精神 team spirit'，属答非所问。  借用原文：greater trust on teams 

 C) 原词陷阱 It helps to resolve problems. 利用第 1 段 how to approach policies, programs or problems 里的 problems 一词，但那是说大家对如何处理问题有分歧（冲突的来源），并非说冲突能'解决问题'，是偷换概念。  借用原文：how to approach policies, programs or problems 

 D) 原词陷阱 It facilitates policy-making. 把第 1 段 approach policies, programs or problems 中的 policies 改头换面成 policy-making，但原文从未说冲突有助于'制定政策'，是无中生有的作用。  借用原文：how to approach policies, programs or problems
questions.spoken_text: Why is productive conflict important for teams and organizations?

questions.prompt: What does productive conflict need as a basis?
options: An innovative mind.
Corporate culture.
Mutual trust.
A healthy mentality.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 What does productive conflict need as a basis? 

 【翻译】 建设性冲突需要什么作为基础? 
 A)  创新思维。 
 B)  企业文化。 
 C)  相互信任。 
 D)  健康的心态。 

 【答案】 C （细节题） Mutual trust. 
 【定位】 P4 But if you're in a place where you have a basis of trust, conflict can be extremely productive. 
 但如果你处在一个有信任基础的环境里，冲突可以变得极富成效。 

 【信号】 a basis of 直接点前提 。答案信号就是题干同款词 basis：if you're in a place where you have a basis of trust，a basis of 后面紧跟的 trust 正是冲突变得有益所需的基础，与设问的 as a basis 直接对上。 

 【替换】 a basis of trust ↔ Mutual trust. 核心词同+补足限定 

 【排除】 A) 原词陷阱 An innovative mind. 盗用原文多次出现的 innovative/innovation，但创新在原文里是冲突带来的'结果'（lead to increased innovation），不是它需要的'基础'，前提与结果被颠倒。  借用原文：It can lead to increased innovation 

 B) 未提及 Corporate culture.（企业文化）原文从未提及，是借'谈职场就该有企业文化'的常识硬塞的，与 basis of trust 无关。 
 D) 原词陷阱 A healthy mentality. 盗用原文 good leaders and healthy teams 里的 healthy，但那是形容'健康的团队'，而非冲突所需的'健康心态 mentality'，原文也没说前提是某种心态，是张冠李戴。  借用原文：good leaders and healthy teams
questions.spoken_text: What does productive conflict need as a basis?
